Reference comparisons

Town Square vs Stardew Valley world density

Under blind A/B review. Buildings, props and NPC routines have landed; the open ground between districts is the current gap.

Festival Plaza vs Stardew Night Market

The event transformation reads: string lights, bunting, a lit ceremonial carpet, stalls and a gathered crowd. Trial lanterns still need mounts.

Current critic findings

SevAreaFinding
blocker Rendering Phaser getFrame() returns the __BASE frame for unknown names, so every missing-art guard was drawing the entire 2048px atlas across the scene.
major Terrain Tile families were keyed by leaf name, so tile/woods/grass_* merged with tile/town/grass_* and the town field rendered as a two-tone checkerboard.
major Terrain edgePixels treated a tile's own border as a material edge, putting a lit line on the top row of every interior tile — a horizontal band across every path and every water surface in the game.
major Terrain Grass variants were tone-mismatched and non-periodic, producing per-tile seams and brightness checkerboarding. Now seamless and rank-quantised.
minor Terrain Flagstone stamped one identical stone pattern on every tile; now a per-tile cellular partition with the mortar groove and lit bevel on separate pixels.
major Build One agent's in-progress edit broke every other agent's art build. Modules now load dynamically and a broken one is skipped and reported.
major Build The hand-maintained map import list was a shared file every map author had to edit; one stale import broke the whole game. Maps and areas are now discovered by glob.
major Lumen Vale Building footprints render as bare brown rectangles extending past the building sprites; ground under a building should match its surroundings.
major Lumen Vale Town Square flagstone is one uniform slab and density falls off sharply outside it; flowerbed prop repeats too evenly across open grass.
minor Festival The three trial lanterns read as floating; they need visible mounts so their role is legible before the trial starts.
